title: Short Stuff: The Shortest War
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896, often cited as the shortest war on record. Josh and Chuck explain Zanzibar's role as a wealthy trading port, including the slave trade run through it, and the 1890 British-German treaty tied to the Scramble for Africa. Britain made Zanzibar a protectorate and installed Hamad bin Thuwaini as a puppet sultan in 1893. After his death, Khalid bin Barghash seized the throne for three days. The next morning, after a British ultimatum, Royal Navy ships shelled the palace; the war lasted roughly 38 to 45 minutes, with about 500 Zanzibari deaths and one British sailor wounded. Barghash fled to the German consulate. Britain then installed a new sultan. Zanzibar became independent in December 1963 and later merged with Tanganyika to form Tanzania. The episode also includes a Billy Joel tangent and a mention of an unrelated GI Joe reference.

segments.title: Introduction and the shortest war
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode on the Anglo-Zanzibar War and note its very short duration, estimated at 38 to 45 minutes.

segments.title: Zanzibar as a trading port
segments.summary: Zanzibar was a wealthy trading hub between the African interior and the Middle East and Europe. Chuck gives a Billy Joel digression and Josh a GI Joe reference.

segments.title: Trade and the slave trade
segments.summary: Zanzibar exported ivory, spices, and enslaved Africans, with up to about 30,000 people shipped out through the port into the 1880s.

segments.title: Britain, Germany, and the Scramble for Africa
segments.summary: Britain was interested in controlling the port and ending slavery. A 1890 British-German treaty divided East Africa, part of the Scramble for Africa and European colonization of the continent.

segments.title: British protectorate and puppet sultan
segments.summary: Zanzibar became a British protectorate, and Britain installed Hamad bin Thuwaini as a friendly sultan in 1893. After his death, his nephew or cousin Khalid bin Barghash, who had earlier tried to take the throne, seized power, likely by poisoning.

segments.title: Barghash takes the throne for three days
segments.summary: Barghash declared himself sultan right after Thuwaini's death, and the British refused to accept him, creating a standoff.

segments.title: British ultimatum and gunboat diplomacy
segments.summary: The British pointed warship cannons at the palace and gave an ultimatum to leave by 9 a.m. Barghash, backed by his own armed force of thousands of defenders, refused to leave, and the British consul Basil Cave said Britain would fire if he did not comply.

segments.title: The bombardment and Barghash's escape
segments.summary: At 9 a.m. British ships fired on the palace from three warships. Within about two minutes Barghash fled to the German consulate and was smuggled to German-held Tanzania.

segments.title: Casualties and aftermath
segments.summary: About 500 Zanzibaris died while only one British sailor was wounded. Britain then installed a new, more compliant sultan.

segments.title: Independence and merger into Tanzania
segments.summary: Zanzibar became a sovereign state and Commonwealth member on 10 December 1963, then merged with Tanganyika to form Tanzania. The hosts reflect on the Scramble for Africa and African history.
